step.name: Step 1: Define Your Vision and Budget
step.text: Start by clearly outlining what you hope to achieve with the addition – the purpose, the desired size, and how it will integrate with your existing home. Simultaneously, establish a realistic budget, including a contingency for unforeseen issues. This initial clarity helps guide all subsequent decisions and ensures your project stays on track financially.

step.name: Step 2: Understand Zoning and Property Constraints
step.text: Before any design work begins, you need to understand local zoning regulations. This includes researching setbacks, lot coverage limits, height restrictions, and other requirements specific to your property in areas like San Marino, Pasadena, or throughout the San Gabriel Valley. LineWork Development assists with this by gathering current property information or conducting a survey, as these restrictions significantly impact what's possible.

step.name: Step 3: Develop Architectural Plans and Engineering Documents
step.text: This is where your vision takes shape on paper. Architectural plans will detail the layout, aesthetics, and functionality of your new space. If your addition involves major structural changes or a new foundation, structural engineering documents will be required to ensure safety and compliance. This phase is critical for getting approvals and ensuring a buildable design.

step.name: Step 4: Navigate the Permitting Process
step.text: Once plans are finalized, permit applications are submitted to the local building department. This involves a plan review process where authorities check for compliance with building codes, energy requirements, and other regulations. Don't start construction until all required approvals are issued – this is a common mistake that can cause significant delays and penalties. The timing for this can vary, but patience here is key.

step.name: Step 5: Construct the Addition and Pass Inspections
step.text: With permits in hand, construction begins. This typically involves preparing the site, laying the foundation, framing the structure, installing the roof, connecting utilities, and completing interior finishes. Throughout this phase, staged inspections will occur to ensure each stage of construction meets code. Your contractor will coordinate these inspections, leading to final approval.

step.name: Step 6: Final Walkthrough and Project Completion
step.text: After all construction is complete and inspections are passed, you'll have a final walkthrough with your design-build team. This is your chance to review the finished space, ensure everything meets your expectations, and address any remaining punch-list items.
